Questions.QuestionText: What breed of dog is pictured here?
Questions.AnswerFact: The German Shorthaired Pointer (or Deutsch Kurzhaar) is of medium size, and is an all-purpose gun dog suitable for hunting and retrieving on both land and water.

Questions.QuestionText: How many teeth does an adult dog typically have?
Questions.AnswerFact: Adult dogs typically have 42 teeth arranged in a pattern optimised for their omnivorous diet. Their teeth consist of 12 incisors, 4 canines, 16 premolars and 10 molars.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following dog breeds is typically the smallest in size?
Questions.AnswerFact: Chihuahuas are considered the world's smallest dog breed, usually standing about 6-9 inches tall. While other small breeds like Pomeranians and Shih Tzus are also tiny, the Chihuahua is consistently the smallest on average.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following dog breeds is typically the largest in size?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Irish Wolfhound is often recognized as the tallest dog breed in the world (usually fighting for this title against the Great Dane). The Irish Wolfhound often stands over 30 inches at the shoulder.

Questions.QuestionText: How old was the world's oldest verified dog when they died?
Questions.AnswerFact: The world record for oldest verified dog is held by Bluey, a female Australian Cattle Dog who lived to be 29 years 5 months old (1910-1939). A Portuguese dog named Bobi briefly took the record (31 years 5 months, 1992-2023), but in 2024 Guinness World Records revoked the claim due to doubts about his true age.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the dog Laika best known for?
Questions.AnswerA: Being the first dog to appear in a televised dogfood advert
Questions.AnswerB: Being the first dog to reach the peak of Mt. Everest
Questions.AnswerC: Being the first dog in space to orbit the Earth
Questions.AnswerD: Being the first dog in a submarine 100m below sea level
Questions.AnswerFact: Laika was a Soviet space dog who became the first animal to orbit the Earth aboard Sputnik 2 on 3 November 1957. Prior to Laika, other animals including monkeys and dogs had been sent on suborbital flights, but Laika was the first to complete an orbit. Unfortunately, she did not survive the mission.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the fastest dog breed on land?
Questions.AnswerFact: The fastest dog breed is the Greyhound, with a top recorded speed of 45mph (72km/h). The Afghan Hound, Saluki and Sloughi all have a recorded top speed of 42mph (68km/h).

Questions.QuestionText: What is the scientific name for the Labrador Retriever?
Questions.AnswerFact: There is no separate scientific name for individual dog breeds. All domestic dogs, including the Labrador Retriever, belong to the same subspecies: Canis Lupus Familiaris, meaning “domestic dog”. Modern breeds differ in appearance and behaviour, but they are all genetically the same species.

Questions.QuestionText: How many dog breed groups are recognised in the UK?
Questions.AnswerFact: The UK Kennel Club recognises 7 breed groups: Hound, Working, Terrier, Gundog, Pastoral, Utility and Toy. Other organisations classify breeds slightly differently, the American Kennel Club also recognises 7 groups (with name differences), while the Fédération Cynologique Internationale recognises 10.

Questions.QuestionText: According to the Dogs Trust National Dog Survey 2025, what was the most popular name for male dogs in the UK?
Questions.AnswerFact: According to the Dogs Trust National Dog Survey 2025, Teddy was the most popular male dog name in the UK with 2,750 dogs. Milo followed with 2,711, Alfie with 2,487, and Buddy with 2,480.

Questions.QuestionText: Which breed of dog was the first to be successfully cloned?
Questions.AnswerFact: The first successfully cloned dog was an Afghan Hound named Snuppy, created by scientists in South Korea in 2005. The clone was carried by a Labrador Retriever surrogate after many failed attempts. In later research, additional clones of Snuppy were produced to study the long-term health effects of cloning.

Questions.QuestionText: Which breed of dog has the strongest recorded bite force?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Turkish Kangal is widely reported to have the strongest bite force of any domestic dog breed, measured at around 743 PSI. Turkish Kangals were bred to protect flocks from large predators such as wolves and bears.
